names.iupac: N,α-dimethylbenzeneethanamine (as given by EUDA); the INN refers to the (S)-enantiomer, (S)-N,α-dimethylbenzeneethanamine
cas: 7632-10-2: N,α-dimethylbenzeneethanamine without stereo designation (NIST's other names include (±)-methamphetamine and DL-methamphetamine)

forms.detail: The most common salt (CAS 51-57-0); occurs as a white or off-white powder or as crystals soluble in water.
Methamphetamine base is a colourless volatile oil, insoluble in water (EUDA). AIHW lists base as one of the three forms in which methamphetamine is commonly found in Australia.

Illicit products mostly consist of powders (EUDA profile). In the EU market analysis (2022), powder is methamphetamine hydrochloride mixed with other ingredients such as lactose, dextrose or caffeine. AIHW: powder, known as 'speed' (Australia).

The pure crystalline hydrochloride is known as 'ice' (EUDA profile); the EU market analysis (2022) refers to crystal methamphetamine known as 'ice' or 'crystal meth'; AIHW lists a crystalline form, 'ice' or 'crystal' (Australia).
Tablets containing methamphetamine may carry logos similar to those seen on MDMA and other ecstasy tablets.

The EU market analysis (2022) refers to smuggling of methamphetamine or ephedrine in liquid form; the European Drug Report 2026 states that Türkiye reported 60 300 methamphetamine seizures in 2024, amounting to 25.9 tonnes and 7 904 litres.

forms.form: Enantiomers (d- and l-, S- and R-)
forms.detail: The asymmetric α-carbon gives two enantiomers, formerly called the (+)- or d- and the (−)- or l-stereoisomer and now defined as S and R (EUDA). CAS 537-46-2 is the (S)-(+)-enantiomer and 33817-09-3 the (R)-(−)-enantiomer, levmetamfetamine (NIST). INCB lists metamfetamine, metamfetamine racemate and levomethamphetamine as separate entries.

forms.form: l-isomer (levmetamfetamine) in nasal decongestant inhalers (United States)
forms.detail: Levmetamfetamine is the active ingredient of over-the-counter nasal decongestant inhalers marketed under the OTC monograph (DailyMed label, marketing category 'OTC Monograph Drug', M012) and is listed as a topical nasal decongestant in 21 CFR 341.20(b)(1); 21 CFR 1308.22 lists such inhalers among nonnarcotic products excluded from all schedules.

Desoxyn (methamphetamine hydrochloride) tablets, NDA 005378, marketing status Prescription (Drugs@FDA). Generic labels on DailyMed give the chemical name as (S)-N,α-dimethylbenzeneethanamine hydrochloride.

drug_checking.finding: Opioids were detected in 3.5% (34 of 972) of samples expected to be methamphetamine. Across 8,889 samples not expected to contain an illicit opioid (fentanyl, heroin or nitazene), 189 (2%) contained one, most of them (61.4%) at trace concentration (below 0.50% wt/wt).
drug_checking.where_when: Substance Drug Checking, British Columbia, Canada; samples collected 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023 (published 2025)

drug_checking.finding: Among 103 samples bought from cryptomarkets, all 5 sold as methamphetamine (and all 24 sold as MDMA and all 4 sold as heroin) contained no other substance that the method could detect (infrared spectroscopy, which cannot reliably detect substances below about 5% of the sample, plus fentanyl and benzodiazepine test strips); 5 samples are too few to show how often this holds.
drug_checking.where_when: Australia (samples bought from cryptomarkets), tested by the Vancouver-based Get Your Drugs Tested service; Test4Pay forum data from 1 September 2022 to 23 August 2023 (published 2024)

drug_checking.finding: Substitution: of the 33 samples expected to be MDMA, 10 contained no MDMA, and 3 of those 10 contained methamphetamine ('crystal Meth') instead.
drug_checking.where_when: One outdoor electronic music festival near Mexico City, Mexico (the paper gives no name, venue or date); 51 samples from 40 people tested on site; published 2023
